details:
The Missão Ipê team developed an educational browser game for the Space Mission Design Game challenge. Players design and simulate missions to five destinations: the International Space Station (ISS), the Moon, Mars, Europa, and Bennu. They select a launch vehicle, spacecraft systems, and scientific instruments, then balance payload mass, power, budget, and mission duration. The simulator evaluates their design and gives them feedback they can use to revise it before launch.

The first mission, Pulso Orbital, was inspired by a real incident documented by NASA. In 2015, an alarm raised concerns about a possible ammonia leak aboard the ISS. The crew sheltered in the Russian segment while controllers investigated. An onboard air quality monitor helped determine that ammonia was not detected, and further tests confirmed the result. In our fictional mission, players decide what equipment to bring to investigate the station’s air quality. NASA-published launch vehicle capacities also inform the game’s payload limits. The game identifies simplified values such as instrument costs and science scores as simulation parameters.

The creative premise is that what you discover depends on what you bring. In Pulso Orbital, a spacecraft with one air quality monitor can be cleared to launch with a science score of 67%, below the mission’s 95% target. Adding a second monitor raises the score to 100% in the simulation, while adding 48 kilograms and occupying another payload slot. This gives players a reason to reconsider a design that can already fly.

We built the prototype in Figma Make and deployed it on Vercel. It runs in a web browser. We designed the experience for students without prior aerospace training, using visible constraints, immediate feedback, and the opportunity to try again. Our goal is to help learners practice explaining why a design serves a scientific objective. Internal testing covered the ISS mission flow. A next step is to test with students and educators and observe whether players recognize the trade-offs and can explain their decisions.
